summary: A schedule or timeline laid out by the server: name intervals (start, end, label, optional lane such as a person or room, optional category for the colour) and it packs overlapping ones into rows, draws a time axis with ticks, a legend for the categories, and a red now line that can follow the device clock. Labels show in full, as an initial, beside a short bar, or not at all, by the space each bar gets.

items.doc: [{"start": "Mon 09:00", "end": "Mon 17:00", "label": "Day", "lane": "Alice", "category": "Day"}] or [start, end, label, lane]. Times: numbers, "HH:MM", "Mon 09:00" (a week from Monday) or "2026-11-02[T09:00]", all the same form. An end before its start runs past midnight; what falls outside the axis is cut

lanes.doc: Lane names in display order (default: order of first use); a lane with no items still gets a row

start.doc: Axis start, same form as the items (default: the earliest start, rounded down to a tick)

end.doc: Axis end (default: the latest end, rounded up). "Sun 24:00" ends a week

now.doc: The now line: a time, "clock" (follows the device clock: for HH:MM, week and date axes), or an expression in hours from the axis origin. Left out: no line

colors.doc: Not a list: an object mapping a category to a theme colour name, e.g. {"Night": "secondary"}. Default: categories take primary, secondary, success, warning, error in order

legend.doc: A row naming the categories under the axis (each swatch shows the initial a narrow bar shows)

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window: only used to choose labels, the bars follow the layout

fontSize.doc: Label size; bars are 1.9 times as tall

description.doc: Spoken summary (lane names and bar labels are read anyway)

pitfalls: Write every time in one form: "Mon 09:00" and "09:00" can't mix
Its height is its content (axis, rows, legend): put it in a scrolling column if there are many lanes
In a week view on a phone, an 8-hour bar is about 12 dp wide: labels give way to the category initial or nothing, so use category (and the legend) for what matters
now: "clock" uses weekDay() and timeInMin(): a week axis must start on Monday 00:00 for the line to land right
About 120 to 250 B per interval (two texts: the full label and its initial) plus the axis
